title: Circuits II
description: Develop fluency with AC circuit analysis, power, coupled circuits, frequency response, filters, Laplace methods, and transfer functions.

topics.title: Phasors and Impedance
topics.description: This section converts sinusoidal time-domain signals into complex-number form. The point is to make capacitors and inductors behave like frequency-dependent impedances so AC circuits can be solved with familiar linear algebra.

children.title: Sinusoidal representation
children.description: Students learn how amplitude, phase, angular frequency, and time shifts map into phasor notation.

children.title: Euler form, rectangular form, and polar form
Complex impedance
children.description: Students learn how resistors, capacitors, and inductors behave in sinusoidal steady state.

children.title: Admittance and equivalent networks
children.description: Students build faster methods for series-parallel AC simplification.

children.title: Measurement and interpretation
children.description: Students connect phasors to lab instruments and real waveforms.

children.title: RMS meters and complex impedance estimation

topics.title: AC Steady-state Analysis
topics.description: This section applies the full Circuits I toolkit to AC networks. Students learn that nodal, mesh, Thevenin, Norton, and superposition methods still work once impedances and phasors are used consistently.

children.title: Nodal analysis with phasors
children.description: Students solve AC circuits by writing KCL equations in the frequency domain.

children.title: Mesh analysis with phasors
children.description: Students solve loop-current problems where voltage sources and series impedances dominate.

children.title: Source transformations and equivalents
children.description: Students simplify AC circuits without losing terminal behavior.

children.title: Thevenin and Norton equivalents in AC
Simulation and lab comparison
children.description: Students learn to check hand analysis against practical tools.

topics.title: AC Power (Real, Reactive, Apparent)
topics.description: Power in AC circuits requires more than multiplying voltage and current magnitudes. Students learn how real work, stored energy exchange, and source loading appear in complex power calculations.

children.title: Instantaneous and average power
children.description: Students see how power varies through the sinusoidal cycle.

children.title: Complex power quantities
children.description: Students learn the engineering meanings of P, Q, S, and power factor.

children.title: Power-factor correction
children.description: Students learn why utilities and industrial systems care about reactive power.

children.title: Efficiency, current reduction, and voltage regulation
Measurement and safety
children.description: Students connect calculations to wattmeters and safe AC practice.

topics.title: Three-phase Circuits
topics.description: Three-phase analysis introduces the dominant architecture of electric power systems. The goal is to understand balanced systems first, then recognize what changes when loads or sources are not ideal.

children.title: Balanced three-phase sources
children.description: Students learn the geometry and notation of three sinusoidal phases.

children.title: Balanced loads
children.description: Students solve common wye and delta load configurations.

children.title: Unbalanced and neutral effects
children.description: Students learn why real distribution systems need careful current accounting.

children.title: Applications
children.description: Students connect theory to power delivery and machines.

children.title: Transformer banks and industrial power panels

topics.title: Magnetically Coupled Circuits
topics.description: This section explains circuits that interact through magnetic fields rather than direct wiring. Students learn how mutual inductance and transformer action support power conversion, isolation, impedance matching, and sensing.

children.title: Mutual inductance
children.description: Students learn how one coil's changing current induces voltage in another.

children.title: Coupled-circuit equations
children.description: Students write circuit equations that include mutual terms.

children.title: Ideal transformers
children.description: Students learn the first-order model for voltage, current, and impedance transformation.

children.title: Nonideal transformer behavior
children.description: Students understand why real components depart from ideal models.

topics.title: Frequency Response
topics.description: Frequency response shows how a circuit treats different sinusoidal inputs. Students learn to describe gain, phase shift, resonance, bandwidth, and selectivity as design and diagnostic tools.

children.title: Response definitions
children.description: Students learn what magnitude and phase response mean physically.

children.title: RC, RL, and RLC behavior
children.description: Students analyze common first- and second-order circuit responses.

children.title: Bandwidth and cutoff
children.description: Students identify the useful operating range of circuits.

children.title: Experimental frequency sweeps
children.description: Students learn how response is measured.

topics.title: Bode Plots
topics.description: Bode plots compress frequency response into a readable engineering sketch. Students learn to predict behavior from poles and zeros and to communicate circuit performance across decades of frequency.

children.title: Magnitude plots
children.description: Students learn log-scale gain representation.

children.title: Phase plots
children.description: Students learn how poles and zeros affect phase.

children.title: Pole-zero interpretation
children.description: Students connect algebraic factors to physical circuit behavior.

children.title: Design reading skills
children.description: Students use plots to judge whether a circuit meets specifications.

topics.title: Passive and Active Filters
topics.description: Filtering turns frequency-response theory into a design tool. Students learn to choose circuit structures that pass wanted frequencies, reject unwanted frequencies, and condition signals before later stages.

children.title: Passive filter structures
children.description: Students understand simple filters built from R, L, and C elements.

children.title: Active filter structures
children.description: Students use op-amps to improve gain, buffering, and design flexibility.

children.title: Filter specifications
children.description: Students translate application needs into design numbers.

children.title: Implementation checks
children.description: Students learn that designed filters must be verified.

children.title: Simulation, breadboard testing, and measurement comparison

topics.title: Laplace Transform Analysis
topics.description: The Laplace transform lets students analyze circuits before they settle into steady state. It unifies transient response, initial conditions, forcing functions, and s-domain impedance methods.

children.title: Transform basics
children.description: Students learn the operational rules needed for circuit analysis.

children.title: S-domain circuit elements
children.description: Students represent R, L, and C components directly in the s-domain.

children.title: Transient response
children.description: Students solve step, impulse, and switched-circuit problems.

children.title: Practical use
children.description: Students connect s-domain analysis to simulation and design.

topics.title: Transfer Functions
topics.description: Transfer functions describe how a circuit maps an input to an output. This final topic ties together filters, frequency response, transients, poles, zeros, stability, and design specifications.

children.title: Input-output modeling
children.description: Students define the quantity a circuit is meant to transform.

children.title: Deriving H(s)
children.description: Students learn several ways to obtain transfer functions.

children.title: Poles, zeros, and stability
children.description: Students infer behavior from the denominator and numerator.

children.title: Design and validation
children.description: Students use transfer functions to meet requirements and test results.
